best_for: Students, bug bounty beginners and developers learning web security who want to intercept and replay HTTP traffic by hand without paying.

points.title: The manual tools are all here
points.text: Community includes the intercepting proxy for HTTP and WebSockets, proxy history, Repeater, Decoder, Sequencer and Comparer.

points.title: No scanner, no saved projects
points.text: The vulnerability scanner, saved project files, full Intruder (Community gets a demo), search, Burp Collaborator testing and automatic crawling are Professional only.

points.title: What Professional costs
points.text: Professional is a per-user subscription, listed at USD 499 on its product page and sold in terms of one or more years. Everyone who uses it needs their own subscription. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Give it memory
points.text: PortSwigger lists 4 GB of RAM as the minimum for basic proxying and 16 GB as recommended, with 1 GB of disk for the install.

points.title: Windows here lags behind
points.text: The Windows listing tops out at 2026.3.3, while macOS and Linux are at 2026.11.2. Get newer Windows builds from PortSwigger's site. Windows keeps 136 versions; macOS and Linux only the current release.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not verified
points.text: The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and Arm64, is not marked verified on Flathub. Burp's embedded browser does not work on Windows 7, 8 or 8.1.
